title: Tenant Profile
description: Definition of a tenant and the user's role within it.

assigned_role.description: The user's primary role in this tenant (e.g., strategist, pm, lead).

allow_cross_distillation.description: Allow only explicitly brokered, redacted promotion to a broader tier.

knowledge_root.description: Repo-relative tenant knowledge root (DA-01). Defaults to knowledge/confidential/{tenant_slug} when omitted.

ingest_sources.description: Ingest source systems declared for this tenant (DA-01).

provider_attestations.description: Per-provider statement of how this tenant's account is contracted, for the tier x egress gate. It governs both confidential and personal material: both may leave the machine only for a provider that does not train on them. Training use is a property of the plan that was purchased, not of the provider id, and different tenants can be on different plans — so the claim belongs here, next to the account it describes. Absent or expired is treated as 'unknown' and fails closed. Tier decides whether the question arises at all: material a tenant is happy to have trained on — open-source work, for example — belongs at the public tier, where the gate fails open and no attestation is needed. Attest here only for material that is genuinely confidential.

training_use.description: Whether the vendor trains on material sent under this plan.

plan.description: The purchased plan this attestation covers (e.g. 'api-paid', 'team', 'free'). The same provider id behaves differently per plan, so an attestation without one is hard to re-check.

basis.description: Where the claim was verified: terms URL, contract reference or ticket. A 'none' claim with no basis is an assertion, not a fact.

attested_by.description: Who made the claim. This is an accountable statement, not a configuration value.

attested_at.description: When it was verified. Vendor terms and purchased plans both change, so this decays.

expires_at.description: When re-verification is due. Defaults to attestation_ttl_days from the egress policy.
